hook.text: Make a chat with a model twice as long, and its bill roughly triples.

why.text: [curious] So why doesn't it just double?

memory.text: Because the model keeps no memory between turns. So every turn, the app sends the whole chat again, from the top.

first.text: Turn one sends a two-thousand-token system prompt and your first message.

second.text: Turn two sends all of that again, plus the reply and your next message. That's five hundred fifty new tokens.

climb.text: Every turn resends the last one and adds a slice, so the requests climb like a staircase.

forty.text: By turn forty, one request is twenty-three thousand six hundred tokens.

area.text: You pay for every one of those bars. So the bill is the area under the staircase, plus the replies.

split.text: Cut that area in two. The bottom is a rectangle: the system prompt, the same every turn.

triangle.text: On top sits a triangle: the chat itself, sent again and again.

double.text: Now double the turns. The rectangle just gets twice as long.

four.text: But the triangle gets twice as long and twice as tall, so four of the old one fit inside.

bills.text: On Sonnet, ten turns cost thirteen cents. Twenty, thirty-seven and a half. Forty, a dollar nineteen.

ratios.text: That's two point eight times, then three point two. Eighty turns would be three and a half.

toward.text: The longer the chat, the more of the bill is triangle, so each doubling creeps toward four times.

cache.text: Prompt caching goes after the triangle. You still send it all, but whatever you sent last turn is read back at a twentieth of the price.

flat.text: Only the new slice pays in full, so the staircase flattens. Forty turns drop from a dollar nineteen to twenty-six cents.

stable.text: So put whatever never changes first, where the cache can match it.

fresh.text: And when a chat runs long, start a fresh one. Eight five-turn chats cost forty-two cents. One forty-turn chat, a dollar nineteen.

end.text: A chat grows by one slice a turn. Its bill grows by the whole chat.
